The truth is that the earth was in need of a new prophethood. Corruption and mischief had spread everywhere across it, and the condition of the world's religions was such that their reform had become impossible. A new religion and a new prophethood were needed; a fresh movement and a new system were needed. Disbelief had permeated the beliefs and ideas of the people of the earth: whether the People of the Book, who had been given a true heavenly religion but who, after knowing it, forgot it and made complete distortions in the religion, or the polytheists of the Arabian Peninsula and the polytheists outside it. Both had entered into a state of disbelief.

They had reached such a point of disbelief and distortion that a return from it was not possible for them. Their reform could be achieved only through a new religion, only through a messenger who is himself a clear proof, and who has with him a Book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood.
Messenger ................................ purified (98:2) "(That is) a Messenger from Allah reciting purified scriptures." These scriptures are free from polytheism and disbelief.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 98, verse 3:

﴿Therein are upright books﴾ (98:3), "in which are written entirely straight and correct writings." The word "kitab" (book) is also used for a subject or topic, for example Kitab al-Taharah (the Book of Purification), Kitab al-Salah (the Book of Prayer) and Kitab al-Qadr (the Book of Destiny), Kitab al-Qiyamah. The purified scrolls (suhuf mutahharah) refer to this Qur'an, in which there are upright books, that is, subjects and issues. This is why this Message and this Messenger came at the most appropriate time, and these scrolls, these surahs and these subjects of discourse and issues came so that they might bring about such a revolutionary reform on earth as no other form of reform was possible. Why did the world need this Messenger, this message and this book in that age? I will answer this with an excerpt from the book "The Effect of the Rise and Fall of Muslims on the Human World" by the great Islamic thinker Sayyid Abul Hasan Ali Nadwi. This excerpt is very brief and clear on the subject. In the first chapter, first section, he writes:

The sixth century CE was, without any disagreement, the darkest and lowest period of human history. For centuries humanity had been moving towards a depth and decline, and it had reached its final point, and there was no power on the face of the earth that could take hold of falling humanity and stop it from falling into the cave of destruction. The condition of humanity was such that, as it went towards decline, its speed was increasing day by day. In this century, man had become forgetful of God and had completely become forgetful of himself. He was entirely unconcerned, unaware of his end, and utterly deprived of the ability to distinguish good from bad. The voice of the prophets' call had, for a long time, been suppressed. The lamps that these figures had lit had either been extinguished in the storms of winds, or were flickering in pitch darkness in such a way that only a few God-knowing hearts were illuminated by them. They could not illuminate cities, let alone light up even a few houses fully. Religious people, clasping the trust of religion to their chests, had withdrawn from the arena of life and had taken refuge in monasteries, churches, deserts and caves in solitude, and, avoiding the demands of life's struggle, its harsh and bitter realities, had, having been defeated in the battle between religion and politics, spirituality and materialism, abdicated their duties of leadership. And those who remained in the storm of life had made peace with kings and the people of the world, and their unlawful desires, the oppressive system of government and the oppressive economic system had become their helpers, and they had become partners and sharers with these worldly people in eating the wealth of people and in unlawfully benefiting from their strength and wealth.

"In that age, the great religions had become toys of children, and these religions had become targets for hypocrites. The outward form and inner realities of these religions had been distorted to such an extent that if their founders and propagators could have come to this century and seen what had happened to their religions, they would never have been able to recognise them. In the cradles of civilisation and culture, arrogance, waywardness and moral degradation had arisen, and the result was that all nations had become entangled in their internal disputes and problems. They had neither a message to present to the world nor a call to humanity. In truth, these nations and religions had become thoroughly hollow and feeble from within. The springs of their life had dried up. They had neither religious guidance and teachings, nor any reasonable principles for the system of government."
(Ibid., pp. 37-38 and pp. 39-40)

This rapid glimpse gives a very good and brief picture of the state of the religions of the world before the Prophetic mission of Muhammad (ﷺ). The People of the Book and the polytheists, because of the points by which they entered the borders of disbelief, the Qur'an has repeatedly pointed to them. For example, regarding the Jews and Christians, the Qur'an has stated explicitly:

﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah"﴾ (9:30). And at another place:

﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians have nothing [of value] upon which they stand," and the Christians say, "The Jews have nothing [of value] upon which they stand"﴾ (2:113).

And regarding the Jews, in Surah al-Ma'idah, verse 64, it is:

﴿And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained." Chained be their own hands, and cursed are they for what they have said. Rather, both His hands are extended; He spends however He wills﴾ (5:64). And in al-Ma'idah 72:

﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary"﴾ (5:72), and

﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three"﴾ (5:73).

And regarding the polytheists, in Surah al-Kafirun:

﴿Say, "O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion"﴾ (109:1-6). These and other verses point to the polytheists and other disbelievers.

And as a result of this disbelief, corruption, destruction and decline were widespread throughout the regions of the world. In the words of Maulana Nadwi: "In short, in the seventh century CE there was no nation on the face of the earth that could be called righteous in temperament, nor any society that possessed the high values of nobility and morality, nor any government based on justice, equity and mercy, nor any leadership that possessed knowledge and wisdom, nor any religion in the world that could be called the true religion of the prophets and possessed their teachings and characteristics."

These were the reasons why the mercy of Allah required that He send a Messenger for the guidance of mankind, who would recite pure scrolls, containing the most upright and correct teachings. The truth is that the disbelievers among the polytheists and the People of the Book could in no way have escaped this corruption and this decline except through a new message and such a day.

Here the Holy Qur'an makes clear that the path of deviation which the People of the Book took, or the disputes they created among themselves, was not due to ignorance, nor because the teachings of the divine religion had some complexity or ambiguity. The truth is that correct knowledge had already come to them, the proofs of truth were present with them, and despite this they differed among themselves:

The first divergence occurred among the Jews, before the mission of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him). They broke into pieces and became many sects and parties. Yet their Messenger was one, namely Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him), and their Book was also one, namely the Torah. They had split into five sects, such as the Sadducees (Sadoqiyyah), the Pharisees (Farisi), the Essenes (Asin), the Ghali and the Samaritans (Samiri). Each of these sects had its own beliefs, characteristics and its own direction. When Isa (peace be upon him) was sent, a dispute began between the Jews and the Christians. Yet Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) was the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and he confirmed the Torah. The differences between Jews and Christians grew to such an extent that they took the form of enmity and hostility, and intense hatred arose between the two parties. As a result, the massacres that continued are part of history. It was such a massacre that, when a person reads of these events even today, his hair stands on end.

"At the end of the sixth century, the mutual rivalry and hatred between the Jews and the Christians had reached such a limit that each of them left no stone unturned in humiliating the other party, in taking revenge for their nation from it, and in treating the vanquished in an inhuman manner. In 610 CE, the Jews rioted against the Christians in Antioch. The emperor Phocas sent the famous military officer Bonosus to suppress it. He destroyed the entire population in such a way that thousands were killed by the sword, hundreds were drowned in the river, burned in fire, and thrown before wild beasts, and were thus destroyed." (Duniya aur Musalmanon ke Urooj o Zawal ka Asar, p. 47)

"In the book al-Khitat of al-Maqrizi it is written: During the time of the Roman emperor, the Persian king Khusraw invaded Syria and Egypt. That army demolished the churches of Bayt al-Maqdis, Palestine and Shaak, and killed all the Christians of Syria. Then he came to Egypt in search of Christians, where his army killed Christians in very large numbers and took countless people captive. In this war against the Christians, and in demolishing the churches, the Jews helped the Persians, and they came from Tarbiyah, Jabal, al-Jalil, Qariyah, Nasirah, Sur and the cities of Quds to the Persians, and they took fierce revenge on the Christians and subjected them to torture, slaughter and plunder. In Quds they demolished two of their churches and burned all the houses to ashes. They took away a piece of the holy wood of the cross and took captive the Pope of Quds and many of his companions."

The same author describes the conquest of Quds thus: "Meanwhile the Jews rebelled in the city of Sur. They sent their representatives to other cities. The Jews made pledges to launch a fierce attack on the Christians and to kill them. Then war broke out between the two parties. The Jews, gathering twenty thousand strong, attacked and demolished the churches outside Sur. Thereupon the Christians gathered in large numbers and attacked the Jews. The Jews suffered a crushing defeat and a great number of them were killed. At that time Heraclius became Roman ruler in Constantinople. By a stratagem he devised against the Shah of Iran, he defeated the Iranians, and they left him and departed. After this victory Heraclius set out from Constantinople to set in order the government of Syria and Egypt, and to rebuild what the Iranians had destroyed and ruined. The Jews came from Tarbiyah and presented themselves before Heraclius, offered him precious gifts and asked him for a sworn guarantee of safety. Heraclius gave them a sworn guarantee. After this Heraclius reached Bayt al-Maqdis. The Christians received him with Gospels, crosses, incense and burning torches. Heraclius found the city and its churches ruined, which caused him severe grief.

The Christians told Heraclius how the Jews, together with the Persians, attacked the Christians, killed them and demolished their churches. They also told him that in bloodshed and plunder they were worse than the Persians, and that they left nothing undone in uprooting the Christians. The Christians urged Heraclius to root out the Jews and set out their good aspects before him. Heraclius expressed his inability, saying that he had already granted them safety and had made a sworn promise to them. The priests, popes and elders of the Christians issued a fatwa that there was no sin in killing the Jews, since they had obtained that safety from Heraclius by deception, because Heraclius had not been told what cruelties had been inflicted upon the Christians. They said that as expiation for Heraclius, they would fast one Friday of each year. This fast would be obligatory, and they would make all Christians bound to it. Then Heraclius accepted their word, launched a fierce attack on the Jews and annihilated them. Thus in the Roman empire of Egypt and Syria no Jew remained alive, except those who fled and hid somewhere.

From these narratives it is known that these two peoples, the Jews and the Christians, are hard-hearted, lusting to shed human blood, and that they let no opportunity to destroy an enemy slip from their hands, and in this matter they do not stop at any limit." (Madha Khasira al-Alam, Abu al-Hasan al-Nadwi, pp. 9–11, first edition)

After this, differences began to arise among the Christians, although their Book was one and their Prophet was one. The first differences arose in fundamental beliefs. After that they became sects upon sects. These sects hated one another intensely and became fierce enemies of one another. Differences arose concerning the person and nature of Hazrat Masih (peace be upon him), whether his nature was divine (lahuti) or human (nasuti). Then differences arose concerning the nature of his mother. Then differences arose over the doctrine of the Trinity, that is, tathlith. In their view, God is one of three. The Holy Quran, quoting these beliefs of theirs, has clearly stated that these people have become disbelievers.

﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary."﴾ (5:72)

﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three."﴾ (5:73)

﴿And [mention] when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'"﴾ (5:116)

As a result of these differences arose the most severe dispute, which occurred between the Christians of Syria and the Christians of Rome and Egypt. One party was the Melkite Christians of Rome and Syria, and the other party was the Monophysite sect of Egypt. The Melkite Christians held that the natures of Hazrat Masih consisted of two parts, one divine (malakuti) and the other human (nasuti), whereas the Monophysite Christians of Egypt said that he had a single nature, which vanished in the way a drop of vinegar falls into the sea and is annihilated. In the sixth and seventh centuries this difference grew very intense between these two sects, and it appeared as though these were not two sects but two separate religions, just as Jews and Christians are two separate religious communities, and each considers that the other's religion has no foundation. (Musalmanon ka Urooj o Zawal, Abu al-Hasan Ali al-Nadwi)

"In 628 CE, Heraclius gained victory over the Persians. After this he sought to unite the Christian sects that were at war with one another and in conflict, and to create harmony and reconciliation among them. It was decided that people should refrain from debating the subject of the nature of Hazrat Masih, whether his nature was one or two, and that they should affirm that the will and decree of Allah is one. In early 631 CE it was settled that the Monothelite doctrine would be the official religion of both the state and the church. Heraclius sought to eliminate the various sects and unify them on one creed, and used every stratagem for this, but the Copts of Egypt expressed their disgust with this innovation and distortion, opposed it strongly, and staked their lives to keep their old belief. These people became his enemies. Heraclius again tried to unite the various sects. He stressed that people should unite only on the belief that the will of Allah is one, and that how the will of Allah is executed should not be discussed. He ordered that no debate be held on this subject. He compiled an official message and spread it throughout the regions of the East. Even this could not stop the religious upheaval of Egypt. Upon this he became angry, and for ten years he continued to inflict the most severe cruelty and oppression upon the people of Egypt. The cruelties he committed, when one reads their accounts, make the hair stand on end even today. People were given agonizing punishments, then they were drowned in the river. Torches were lit and placed upon their bodies, until the fat of their bodies melted and fell to the ground. Prisoners were sealed in sacks of sand and cast into the river, and other such horrifying punishments were inflicted." (Madha Khasira al-Alam, Abu al-Hasan al-Nadwi, pp. 3–5)

These differences and enmities among the People of the Book came after the proofs had reached them.

﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after clear evidence had come to them.﴾ (98:4)

But this knowledge and these proofs were of no benefit to them; desire and misguidance kept carrying them further away from the truth. Yet religion, in its original and initial form, was entirely clear, and its beliefs were perfectly plain and lucid.

This principle is the essential foundation of all religions: worship Allah alone, let religion be exclusively for Allah, stay away from shirk (association of partners with Allah) and the people of shirk, establish prayer, and pay zakah.

﴿And that is the upright religion﴾ (98:5). That is, the belief in the human conscience and consciousness must be pure: exclusive worship and servitude to Allah alone, which is founded upon this belief, and spending wealth in the way of Allah, that is, paying zakah. Whoever brings these principles into reality has established his faith, just as the People of the Book were commanded to do. And just as all the Messengers of Allah were commanded to do the same, the religion of all the Messengers and nations is in fact one: the belief is one, on which all the Messengers have been in agreement, and there is no complexity in this belief and practice. It is a belief in which there is no room for division or disagreement. It is extremely clear, pure, simple and easy. Therefore, the beliefs under discussion and dispute among the People of the Book have no connection with Islam, and such things are not part of the religion of Allah.

Before this, proofs had come to these people through their Messengers. After that, these proofs had come again through Muhammad (ﷺ), who recite pure scriptures and present to them beliefs that are clear, simple and easy. Therefore the right path has become clear, and the end of those who persist in disbelief and do not believe has also become clear.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 98, verses 6–7:

Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is the last Messenger, and the religion he has brought is the last religion. Before this, it was the case that whenever humanity went astray and deviated from the path, Allah would send a Messenger. This series continued without interruption, and people were granted respite at intervals so that they could reform themselves. But the decree of Allah's will was that, by sending a comprehensive, all-encompassing and complete religion, He would bring this series of Messengers to an end. This is the final respite. People will either attain salvation by accepting this final religion, or they will be destroyed and ruined by rejecting it. This is because disbelief (kufr) and polytheism (shirk) become the substitute for evil and the symbol of evil, and there is no limit to evil; whereas faith (iman) becomes the substitute for good, and through faith good reaches its utmost extent.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve from among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. They are the worst of creation.﴾ (98:6) This is a definitive ruling, and there is no room for argument or dispute about it. Even though the deeds of the People of the Book and the polytheists may be good in some respects, some of their manners may be admirable and some of their institutions may be beneficial, as long as these people do not attain the reality of faith, and do not believe in this final religion and this final Prophet, this firm ruling stands. We cannot doubt this decisive judgment merely because of some outwardly good deeds of these people, because the deeds of the disbelievers are in reality far removed from the true source of righteousness and goodness, and they are not part of a firm and correct system of life.

﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds are the best of creation.﴾ (98:7) This too is a definitive ruling, leaving no room for dispute or debate. Its condition is also clear, plain and firm; namely, that they must "believe" (iman). It is not enough that they were born in a land that claims to be a Muslim land, or into a household that claims to be a Muslim household, or that someone merely utters a few words. Rather, it must be a faith that becomes manifest in practice within life itself.

﴿And have done righteous deeds﴾. Their faith and their profession of faith must not be mere words and phrases that remain only on the lips. Righteous deeds (salihat) are those actions which Allah has commanded to be performed, including morals, deeds, conduct and dealings. The greatest of these deeds is to establish the Shari'ah of Allah upon the earth, and for judgments among people to be in accordance with the Shari'ah of Allah. Those who do these things are the best of creation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 98, verse 8:

﴿Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever.﴾ (98:8) Such are gardens in whose bounties they will remain forever, and where there will be complete peace, with no fear of their ever being exhausted or coming to an end. The prospect of extinction and the loss of peace and security would spoil the enjoyment of all the comforts and good things of the world. And the flowing of rivers beneath these fresh gardens points to the fact that freshness and springtime in these gardens will be everlasting, and that they will be full of life and beauty.

The context moves a step further in describing this everlasting bounty and mercy.

﴿Allah is well pleased with them, and they are well pleased with Him.﴾ (98:8) This pleasure comes from Allah, and it is higher than all blessings and fresher than all joys. The contentment that exists in the hearts of these believers is itself the pleasure of their Lord. It means that they are content with what divine destiny decides concerning them, content with the favours Allah has bestowed upon them, and content with the relationship that exists between them and Allah. It is a pleasure through which a person feels deep joy, delight and tranquillity. The expression "Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him" is one whose meaning cannot be conveyed in any other words.

﴿That is for the one who fears his Lord.﴾ (98:8) This is a final emphasis: that all of this depends on what a person's relationship with Allah is like, and what the nature of that relationship is. It should be remembered that when the consciousness of fear of God arises in a heart, this consciousness impels a person towards righteousness and restrains him from every kind of deviation. It is this consciousness that removes all the veils from before a person's eyes, and the human heart stands directly before Allah, the One, the Subduer. Because of this consciousness, a person's worship and righteous deeds are purified of every kind of polytheism and show-off. For the one who fears his Lord, his heart becomes empty of fear of other than Allah, and he does not show consideration to anyone else. This consciousness convinces a person that Allah rejects all deeds in which there is any motive other than seeking His pleasure. Allah is the Self-Sufficient King; for Him there must be purely sincere deeds, otherwise He will reject them.

In this short surah, these four great truths have been recorded, and the Qur'an has expressed these truths in its own distinctive style, which stands out very clearly in this surah of a few lines.
